title: Organic and Precision Farming Mock Test

questions.question: Which of the following is/are the major problem in modern agriculture system in India?
questions.explanation: Problems in modern agriculture: Faulty agriculture practices lead to the adverse effects such as loss of fertile top soil through wind and water erosion. Due to improper management of irrigation water, salinization and alkalization of the soil takes place. Approx. 6 m ha of land is affected by water logging and another 7 m ha is salinized due to faulty irrigation practices. Monocropping or especially rice wheat cropping system led to the loss of fertility of the soil and impact the biodiversity of that region. Excessive use of chemical fertilizer, pesticide, weedicide causes pollution of water bodies and ground water resources. Excessive use of ground water for irrigation with faulty irrigation practices causes depletion of the ground water table.[cite: 3]

questions.question: ___ is a balanced management system of the renewable resources including soil, wildlife, forest, crops, fish, livestock, plant genetic resources and ecosystem without degradation
questions.explanation: Sustainable agriculture is a balanced management system of the renewable resources including soil, wildlife, forest, crops, fish, livestock, plant genetic resources and ecosystem without degradation and to provide food, livelihood for the current and the future generations maintaining or improving productivity and ecosystem services.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which of the following is/are the important practices in the sustainable agriculture?

options.c: Tillage practices up to 8cm of the top soil

questions.explanation: Conservation Of Genetic Resource-land races are to be preserved for future generations. Tillage-minimum tillage practices and maintenance of top 8 cm of soil is vital because most of the biological activities. Nutrient Management- use of green manure like sun hemp, dhaincha, are grown and incorporated in soil after 40 days, use of biofertilizer like azolla. Weed Management, Pest Management, Crop Rotation.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which of the following is/are is not a practice under sustainable agriculture?
questions.explanation: Frequent tillage disrupts soil structure, leading to increased soil erosion, loss of organic matter, reduced water infiltration, and disruption of beneficial microbial activity, ultimately harming soil health and long-term crop productivity.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Under which of the following scheme government is promoting organic farming?

options.b: Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region

questions.explanation: The Government has been promoting organic farming: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY), Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region, Bhartiya Prakratik Krishi Paddhati (BPKP).[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which of the following is a principle of zero budget natural farming?
questions.explanation: Components Of Zero Budget Natural Farming: Beejamrit, Jivamrit, Mulching, Whapasa, Plant protection.[cite: 3]

questions.question: What does wasp aims in zero budget natural farming?

It is the soil's microclimate on which soil organisms and roots depend for most of their moisture and some of their nutrients. questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement about the zero-budget natural farming?
questions.explanation: Beejamrit - It is used for seeds, seedlings or any planting material. It is effective in protecting young roots from fungus. Jivamrit- Jivamrit acts as a bio stimulant by promoting the activity of microorganisms in the soil and also the activity of phyllo-spheric microorganisms when spayed on foliage. Mulching - Is defined as covering of soil surface using both live crops and straw (dead plant biomass) to conserve moisture, lower soil temperature around plant roots, prevent soil erosion, reduce runoff and reduce weed growth. Whapasa -Means the mixture of 50% air and 50% water vapour in the cavity between two soil particles. It is the soil's microclimate on which soil organisms and roots depend for most of their moisture and some of their nutrients. Plant protection-This is a natural insecticide prepared from leaves which have specific alkaloids to repel pests. It controls all sucking pests and hidden caterpillars that are present in pods and fruits.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which of the following organization was set up by the govt of India for dealing with the production, export and certification of the organic products in India.
questions.explanation: APEDA- The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) was established by the Government of India under the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority Act passed by the Parliament in December, 1985. The Act (2 of 1986) came into effect from 13th February, 1986.[cite: 3]

questions.question: APEDA comes under which ministry?
questions.explanation: APEDA Comes under ministry of commerce and industry.[cite: 3]

questions.question: ___ body sets out the standards to be followed in the cultivation, harvest, production, processing and trading of organic products.
questions.explanation: National Standards for Organic Production: National Standards for Organic Production (NSOP) — This body sets out the standards to be followed in the cultivation, harvest, production, processing and trading of organic products.[cite: 3]

questions.question: National Programme for Organic Production is the third-party certification for ___ oriented organic products.

options.c: Target both local and export market

questions.explanation: India has two certification system for the organic products both the system is based on common standards but adopt different verification process. National Programme for organic products- for export related standards for organic products. Participatory Guarantee System (PGS)for India: for domestic and local market.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE about the Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) for India?

options.a: PGS comes under ministry of commerce and industry
options.b: PGS is meant only for international exports.
options.c: PGS provide certification to organic products for domestic market

questions.explanation: India has two certification system for the organic products both the system is based on common standards but adopt different verification process. National Programme for organic products- for export related standards for organic products. Participatory Guarantee System (PGS)for India: for domestic and local market.[cite: 3]

questions.question: National Programme for organic production comes under which ministry

options.d: Ministry of forestry and climate change

questions.question: ___ can be defined as the application of principles and technologies to manage spatial and temporal variability associated with all aspects of agricultural production for the purpose of improving crop performance and environment equally
questions.explanation: It is the management approach to the cultivation of the crops by considering spatially and temporal variations in soils, rainfall, and adopting management techniques to reduce cost, efficient use of inputs and reduce environmental pollution.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which of the following is/are the principles of Precision agriculture?

options.a: To understand the variability in both time & space

questions.explanation: Principles of precision farming: First principle is to understand the basic principle of variability in both time and space. Second principle is the timely collection and analysis of the spatial and temporal variant information of crops, soil, and environment by using the relevant information technologies like remote sensing. Third principle underlies with precision agriculture is managing the variability with the site-specific agronomic recommendations.[cite: 3]

questions.question: What is the primary goal of precision agriculture?

options.b: Enhancing crop productivity while minimizing inputs
options.d: Reducing the need for fertilizers altogether

questions.explanation: Precision agriculture aims to optimize farming efficiency by using advanced technologies to reduce input wastage (fertilizers, water, pesticides) while improving crop yield and sustainability.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which of the following technologies is most commonly used in precision agriculture for mapping fields?
questions.explanation: Global Positioning System (GPS) and Geographic Information System (GIS) help farmers analyze field variability, monitor crop health, and optimize input applications for precision farming.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which sensor type is primarily used to measure soil moisture levels in precision farming?
questions.explanation: Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) and capacitive sensors measure soil moisture levels accurately, helping in efficient irrigation management and preventing overwatering or drought stress.[cite: 3]

questions.question: What is the role of drones in precision agriculture?

options.b: Spraying pesticides, monitoring crops, and gathering data

questions.explanation: Drones equipped with cameras and sensors help in aerial field surveillance, pest detection, disease monitoring, and precision pesticide or fertilizer spraying, improving farm efficiency.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Variable Rate Technology (VRT) in precision farming is used for

options.a: Adjusting the speed of tractors based on soil conditions
options.b: Varying the application of inputs like water, fertilizers, and pesticides based on real-time data
options.c: Changing crop types automatically in the field
options.d: Automating the planting of genetically modified crops

questions.explanation: VRT allows farmers to apply inputs (seeds, fertilizers, water, etc.) in varying amounts depending on field conditions, optimizing usage and reducing waste.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which data analysis technique is commonly used in precision agriculture to predict crop yields?
questions.explanation: Machine learning algorithms analyze large datasets from satellite images, IoT sensors, and historical trends to forecast crop yields and improve decision-making.[cite: 3]

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using IoT (Internet of Things) in precision agriculture?

options.c: farmers to remotely control field operations and collect real-time data
options.d: Elimating the need for weather forecasting

questions.explanation: IoT enables smart farming by connecting sensors, drones, and automated machinery to real-time data networks, allowing farmers to monitor soil health, weather, and crop conditions remotely.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Precision agriculture contributes to environmental sustainability by

options.a: Increasing the use of chemical fertilizers
options.c: Reducing waste and optimizing resource usage

questions.explanation: By using data-driven decisions, precision farming minimizes water, fertilizer, and pesticide use, reducing environmental impact while maximizing productivity.[cite: 3]

questions.question: What is a key challenge faced in the implementation of precision agriculture?

options.a: Lack of consumer demand for precision farming products
options.b: High initial costs and need for technical expertise
options.c: Unavailability of farm animals for precision monitoring

questions.question: How does satellite imagery help in precision farming?

options.a: By providing detailed insights into crop health and soil conditions
options.b: By detecting pests at a microscopic level
options.d: By replacing traditional soil testing methods

questions.explanation: Satellites provide real-time data on vegetation health, moisture levels, and soil conditions, allowing farmers to detect issues early and take corrective actions.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which of the following is a major principle of organic farming according to the International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movements (IFOAM)?

options.a: Maximizing synthetic inputs for better yield
options.b: Enhancing soil fertility through synthetic fertilizers
options.c: Use of genetically modified organisms (GMOs) to improve crops
options.d: Maintaining ecological balance through natural methods

questions.explanation: Organic farming follows four key principles: health, ecology, fairness, and care. It avoids synthetic chemicals and GMOs, emphasizing biodiversity, soil health, and environmental sustainability.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT allowed in certified organic farming?
questions.explanation: Organic farming strictly prohibits the use of GMOs. Instead, it relies on traditional seed varieties and natural breeding methods to maintain genetic diversity and soil health.[cite: 3]

questions.question: What is the main role of mycorrhizal fungi in organic farming?

options.d: Acting as a primary decomposer of organic matter

questions.explanation: Mycorrhizal fungi form symbiotic relationships with plant roots, helping them absorb nutrients like phosphorus more efficiently while improving soil structure and plant health.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which organic farming method involves planting specific crops together to enhance growth and pest control?
questions.explanation: Companion planting involves growing mutually beneficial plants together, such as marigolds with tomatoes to repel nematodes, promoting natural pest control and soil health.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Why is crop rotation important in organic farming?

options.a: It allows continuous use of the same fertilizers
options.b: It helps prevent soil erosion by using deep-rooted crops
options.c: It eliminates the need for manual weeding

questions.explanation: Crop rotation improves soil structure, prevents nutrient depletion, and reduces the buildup of pests and diseases, which commonly occur in monoculture farming systems.[cite: 3]

questions.question: What is the main purpose of using neem-based pesticides in organic farming?

options.a: To kill all insects, including beneficial pollinators
options.b: To provide synthetic growth hormones to crops
options.c: To act as a natural insect repellent and growth regulator
options.d: To increase nitrogen content in the soil

questions.explanation: Neem extracts contain azadirachtin, which disrupts insect growth cycles, acting as an eco-friendly pesticide while preserving beneficial insects like bees and ladybugs.[cite: 3]

questions.question: In organic farming, what is the main advantage of using biofertilizers over synthetic fertilizers?

options.a: Biofertilizers improve soil fertility without environmental harm
options.b: Biofertilizers release nutrients instantly like synthetic fertilizers
options.c: Biofertilizers prevent all pests and diseases
options.d: Biofertilizers eliminate the need for crop rotation

questions.explanation: Biofertilizers (e.g., Rhizobium, Azotobacter) provide essential nutrients naturally while improving soil microbial activity and reducing pollution from chemical fertilizers.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which of the following practices in organic farming helps in carbon sequestration and soil enrichment?

options.c: Use of cover crops and green manure

questions.explanation: Cover crops (e.g., clover, legumes) and green manure enhance soil organic matter, improve microbial diversity, and trap atmospheric carbon, reducing greenhouse gas emissions.[cite: 3]

questions.question: How does vermicomposting benefit organic farming?

options.a: It sterilizes the soil, making it disease-free
options.b: It converts organic waste into nutrient-rich compost using earthworms
options.c: It eliminates the need for crop rotation
options.d: It enhances soil acidity to improve plant growth

questions.explanation: Vermicomposting uses earthworms to break down organic matter into humus-rich compost, improving soil fertility and enhancing plant growth without synthetic additives.[cite: 3]

questions.question: Which organic certification standard is globally recognized for ensuring organic product authenticity?
questions.explanation: The USDA Organic certification ensures that agricultural products meet strict organic standards, including non-GMO seeds, sustainable farming practices, and no synthetic chemicals.[cite: 3]
